result.summary: Adds a `getMemoryLoad()` method to the IPC mining interface to query the memory footprint of active block templates held by external clients. `BlockTemplateManager` tracks live templates via non-owning weak references and computes their memory overhead on demand, summing template vector allocations and any referenced transactions that are no longer in the mempool.
result.problem: External IPC clients, such as Stratum v2 template providers, can retain block templates indefinitely. Because templates hold `CTransactionRef` handles, transactions evicted or replaced in the mempool remain pinned in memory without any way for clients or node operators to observe the resulting memory pressure.
evidence: Addresses issue #33899 ('Block template memory management (for IPC clients)')

Commit message notes that 'IPC clients can hold on to block templates indefinitely... Because each template in turn holds CTransactionRefs, transactions that are removed from the mempool will not have their memory freed.'
Author references client-side integration in Stratum v2 template provider pull request stratum-mining/sv2-tp#63.
result.changed_since_previous: Replaced the transaction-level reference-counting map (`TxTemplateMap`) with a registry of live templates using `std::weak_ptr<const CBlockTemplate>`, deduplicating transactions on demand during `GetTemplateMemoryUsage()`. Also refactored `WaitAndCreateNewBlock` to take the previous template by reference.
result.card: Tracks the memory footprint of block templates held by external IPC clients, accounting for template allocations and transactions that remain pinned in memory after leaving the node mempool. BlockTemplateManager tracks active templates via weak pointers and exposes their aggregate non-mempool memory consumption through a new getMemoryLoad() IPC method. This addresses template memory management for external Stratum v2 template providers (issue #33899) so clients can observe memory pressure and release stale templates.

risk.why: A bug in template registration or memory accounting could report inaccurate usage or cause minor lock contention, affecting only IPC mining clients.
